Thanks for the context — quick read and proposed approach below.

1) Defense control: we should avoid unilateral customer control for IP defense. Proposed compromise: customer may elect to assume defense control for third-party IP claims where customer provides full indemnity and agrees to a mutually-approved counsel, but Redwood retains the right to assume control if Redwood reasonably determines customer defense would prejudice Redwood (sample carve: Redwood may assume control if customer refuses counsel with appropriate experience or if the claim seeks equitable relief that implicates Redwood's operations). Also add a cooperation clause (Redwood can participate, and will be kept reasonably informed).

2) Evidence/evidence SLA: 7 business days is tight but doable if the request fits standard evidence package templates. Suggest we supply an "evidence bundle" within 7 business days for initial triage (logs + requestor instructions) and then a fuller handover within 30 days if more forensic work required. Attach evidence-request-template.xlsx as the standard.

3) Insurance and offsets: keep insurance waterfall language but explicitly preserve Redwood's ability to credit insurance proceeds against indemnity, and limit Redwood's obligation to uninsured amounts subject to an outer cap (we should propose a finite cap tied to the order form amount for commercial practicability).

4) Quick drafting points: will propose alternate clause text (attached) — we should present a single redline back to Varuna that follows the compromise above.

I can draft a short compromise redline today if everyone agrees.

-kim

Appreciate the quick turnaround. Business context to weigh in: Varuna is asking for an enterprise-style customer carve (they've committed to a 12-month volume commitment and multi-year pilot). Ben believes they will sign if defense control and the short evidence window are addressed. We can't broadly accept customer-led defense that allows them to control strategy and settle without Redwood's consent (commercial risk).

Suggested path (business + legal compromise):
- Offer: customer may lead defense only if they (i) provide express indemnity for Redwood, (ii) use pre-approved counsel (we maintain right to reasonable consent), and (iii) obtain Redwood's prior written consent to any settlement that imposes ongoing obligations on Redwood.
- Evidence: commit to initial evidence bundle within 7 business days (logs + call transcripts + metadata) and a fuller handover on a reasonable timeline (30 days) for deeper forensics; call out any data subject to export controls / encryption with an exception path.
- Insurance: keep offsets and allow insurance proceeds to reduce indemnity; propose a monetary cap equal to 12 months of committed fees (to be approved by finance).

Kim — please draft the redline using that structure. Rishi — quick flag on IP posture: if we give up defense control in any material way, we should require that the customer indemnity is not limited by customer's own liability caps and that they carry primary insurance for IP claims.

Ben — if this aligns, I can push a commercial concession (1 month credit) to help close.

—Logan
Head of Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference

Team / Sara —

Attached is a clean redline reflecting the compromise Logan outlined. Highlights:
- Customer-led defense permitted for third-party IP claims subject to: express indemnity, counsel reasonably acceptable to Redwood, and Redwood's prior written consent to settlements that impose obligations on Redwood.
- Evidence: Redwood will deliver an initial evidence bundle within 7 business days (operational template attached) and will continue to cooperate for up to 30 days for deeper forensics. Exceptions called out for encrypted data, export-controlled materials, and logs older than the retention window.
- Insurance: indemnity reduced by insurance proceeds; Redwood retains right to offset and will limit its uninsured exposure to a multiple of monthly committed fees (proposed cap inserted in redline).

Sara — if those edits are acceptable to Varuna, we can exchange final signatures and route the order form to DocuSign. Ben — please confirm whether the 1-month credit offer is still on the table; I'll include it in the redline cover note if yes.
